BiblicalUsage: Challah is a cake, usually unleavened and punctured. It is set out for the consecration of Aaron, baked for the meat offering, carried in the basket of the Nazarite, and dealt out by David to every man and woman of Israel when the ark came home.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a cake in Scripture is never only a cake: it is consecration, offering, vow, and homecoming in turn. God feeds His people with the same bread He is offered.
